mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-trend periods (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 1.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS up and UNRATE down, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month suggests accelerating economic demand, which typically precedes equity market optimism and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not positive in > 70% of INDPRO > 2% events (binomial test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months indicates a cooling inflationary pressure, reducing the Fed's need to tighten policy and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During CPIAUCSL < 2% for 3 months, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1%, it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers real discount rates, thereby increasing the present value of equities and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 1-year average during accommodative periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates labor market imbalance that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with rising HOUST and falling UNRATE, SPX returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.1).
